Stars are 3x3 - R11 = 3 is the 4th argument (width) and the stack slot IDA labels nW holds 3 as the 5th (height). Star x = dtoi(amplitude * cos(speed * y * 0.01) + baseX); 1065646817 / 1202590843 is the double 0x3F847AE147AE147B = 0.01 exactly. Both fills take palette slot 0 (MEMORY[0x1472D0]) with index 255; on an 8bpp surface the written byte is the index, so the slot cannot change a titles pixel. The frame counter at state +8 advances, then SoftSurf_DrawBorderAndBlur, Titles_PresentToSoftSurf, Titles_AnimateParticles, Titles_UpdateStars, Titles_DrawCreditLines. The border fill erases rows 0/319 and columns 0/239 AFTER the fills and SoftSurf_BlurPixels (0xa2000) rewrites every interior pixel, so edge ink is gone by the present; that blur leaves a fingerprint 2 cells past a filled block, which is what makes 3x3 measurable (3x1, 1x3 and 2x2 are not).

0x1aa94 BL              Titles_PresentToSoftSurf; PORTED as Titles_PresentToSoftSurf. Copies the titles surface into g_pMainSurface at (0,0), using SoftSurf_GetAlloc (the raw allocation, whose 4-byte header is u16 width then u16 height) as the glyph, so the surface blits itself as a 240x320 indexed glyph. The palette argument is a POINTER: unk_14A2D0 = 0x1472D0 + 0x3000, and aPalette has 1024 bytes per slot, so this is palette slot 12.

0x1aa9c BL              Titles_AnimateParticles; PORTED as Titles_AnimateParticles. Every frame first walks every particle by (target - current) / 15 using the signed divide, with a sign fallback so a gap under 15 still moves exactly one pixel instead of stalling. Then the frame number picks the mode: under 20 the timers run, 21 restores the target pair from the home pair and re-arms the timer to RandU16(30), 20 and 22 through 500 do nothing, 501 through 679 run the timers again, and 680 or more hands over to Titles_LoadScene (0x468cc, still unported). Timer semantics: positive counts down by one; zero sets target x to 230, target y to RandU16(100)+200 and makes the timer -1; a NEGATIVE timer never counts down again and only moves the target, dropping target x by 10 when target y is at least 300 and otherwise raising target y by 10. That is what keeps a particle circling once it has run out of time.

0x1aaa4 BL              Titles_UpdateStars; PORTED as Titles_UpdateStars. Each star advances y by its speed; above 320 it is reborn with x = RandU16(240), y = 0, speed = RandU16(3)+1 and amplitude = RandU16(100)+1. Star records are 16 bytes at g_pTitlesState + 84020: +0 base x, +4 y, +8 speed, +12 amplitude. The count is at +87220. Game_RandU16(n) returns 0..n-1, so the reborn speed is 1..3 and the amplitude is 1..100.

0x1aaac BL              Titles_DrawCreditLines; PORTED as Titles_DrawCreditLines. Same window rule and same '@ means a decimal glyph index' rule as Titles_DrawBackdrop (0x1e630), reached through one shared helper in the port. Differences: the glyph palette is 31 here, the text colour pair is (255,255,255)/(60,60,60), and the scroll comes from this state block at +87228 rather than unk_138E88. Window: scroll >= 320 gives first row (scroll-340)/20 clamped at 0 and spans 36 rows; below that it starts at row 0 and spans scroll/20 rows. Both ends are clamped against unk_157194, the row count.

listing: 0x1e630 PUSH            {R4-R11,LR}; PORTED as Titles_DrawBackdrop in src/pufo/game/pufo_titles.c. A text record whose first character is 0x40 (@) is not text: the rest is a decimal index into the pointer table at 0x1571A0, and that glyph blob is drawn centred instead.
